documents.title: Open Enrollment and Plan Changes
documents.text: Annual open enrollment runs from November 1 through January 15 each plan year. During this window, members may enroll in a new plan, add or remove dependents, or change coverage tiers without a qualifying life event. Changes made by December 15 take effect January 1; changes made by January 15 take effect February 1. Outside open enrollment, plan changes require a qualifying life event such as marriage, birth, adoption, loss of other coverage, or relocation.

documents.title: Prior Authorization Requirements
documents.text: Certain services require prior authorization before care is rendered. These include elective inpatient admissions, advanced imaging (MRI, CT, PET), specialty medications, bariatric surgery, and inpatient rehabilitation. Your provider submits the request; decisions are typically issued within 5 business days for standard requests and 72 hours for urgent requests. Prior authorization is not required for emergency care. Approved authorizations are valid for 90 days unless otherwise noted.

documents.title: Copays and Cost Sharing
documents.text: Cost sharing varies by plan tier and service type. Primary care office visits carry a 25 USD copay; specialist visits are 50 USD. Urgent care visits are 75 USD. Emergency room visits are 250 USD copay, waived if admitted within 24 hours. Telehealth primary care visits are 15 USD. After copays, in-network services apply deductible and coinsurance per your plan summary. Out-of-network services have higher cost sharing and may not count toward the in-network out-of-pocket maximum.

documents.title: Telehealth and Virtual Care
documents.text: Telehealth is available 24/7 for primary care, behavioral health, and dermatology through the member portal or mobile app. Virtual primary care visits cost 15 USD per visit. Behavioral health telehealth visits are 25 USD. On-demand urgent video visits are 40 USD. Telehealth services are covered in all 50 states for members on PPO and HMO plans. Prescriptions issued during telehealth visits may be sent to your preferred in-network pharmacy.

documents.title: Pharmacy and Formulary
documents.text: The standard formulary has four tiers. Tier 1 generic drugs are 10 USD copay for a 30-day supply. Tier 2 preferred brand drugs are 40 USD. Tier 3 non-preferred brand drugs are 75 USD. Tier 4 specialty medications are 20 percent coinsurance up to 250 USD per fill. Mail-order pharmacy offers a 90-day supply at two times the 30-day copay for tiers 1 and 2. Prior authorization may apply to specialty and select brand medications.

documents.title: Mental Health and Substance Use Coverage
documents.text: Mental health and substance use disorder services are covered at parity with medical benefits. Outpatient therapy visits are a 25 USD copay in-network. Inpatient psychiatric care requires prior authorization and is subject to medical necessity review. The plan covers up to 30 outpatient therapy visits per calendar year without additional authorization; additional visits may require clinical review. Crisis line support is available 24/7 at no charge.

documents.title: Preventive Care Benefits
documents.text: In-network preventive services are covered at 100 percent with no copay, deductible, or coinsurance when provided by an in-network provider and billed with appropriate preventive codes. Covered services include annual wellness visits, immunizations, age-appropriate cancer screenings, contraception, and pediatric well-child visits. Preventive colonoscopy is covered; if a polyp is removed during screening, applicable cost sharing may apply to the procedure portion.

documents.title: HMO Plan Overview
documents.text: The HMO plan requires selection of a primary care provider (PCP) who coordinates referrals to specialists. Specialist visits require a PCP referral except for obstetrics, gynecology, and in-network mental health. The annual in-network deductible is 1,500 USD individual or 3,000 USD family. The in-network out-of-pocket maximum is 6,500 USD individual or 13,000 USD family. Out-of-network services are not covered except for emergency care.

documents.title: PPO Plan Overview
documents.text: The PPO plan allows direct access to in-network specialists without a referral. The in-network deductible is 1,000 USD individual or 2,000 USD family. In-network out-of-pocket maximum is 5,500 USD individual or 11,000 USD family. Out-of-network services are covered at 50 percent coinsurance after the out-of-network deductible of 3,000 USD individual. Specialist office visits are a 50 USD copay in-network.

documents.title: Member Portal and Digital Tools
documents.text: Members access claims, ID cards, provider search, and telehealth scheduling through the secure member portal at members.examplehealth.com or the mobile app. First-time users register with their member ID and date of birth. Paper Explanation of Benefits (EOB) can be switched to paperless in account settings. Secure messaging with care coordinators responds within 1 business day. Two-factor authentication is required for account access.

documents.title: Care Navigation and Provider Search
documents.text: Use the provider directory in the member portal to search in-network primary care, specialists, hospitals, and urgent care by ZIP code, specialty, language, and accessibility needs. Care navigators help schedule appointments, explain benefits, and coordinate transitions of care at no additional cost. Call 1-800-555-0142 Monday through Friday 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM local time. For after-hours clinical questions, use the 24/7 nurse advice line.

documents.title: 24/7 Nurse Advice Line
documents.text: Registered nurses are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week at 1-800-555-0199 for clinical guidance, symptom assessment, and help deciding whether to seek emergency, urgent, or primary care. Nurse line consultations are free for all enrolled members. Nurses do not diagnose conditions or prescribe medication but can escalate to an on-call physician for urgent clinical review when appropriate.
